Images

Source: vignettes/images.Rmd
images.Rmd
library(decisions)

Overview

A decision model can look at an image. decide() takes images in the argument image, alone or with text. This vignette shows the image arguments on one task: does a woven pattern have a flaw? It runs three models:

  • Jev, from TypeSafe, with decider_typesafe().
  • The Decisions API of OpenAI, with decider_openai(). Its default model is gpt-6-luna.
  • Clef-Flash, on a local SGLang server, with decider_systemone().

The results below come from live calls. The package saved them in the package folder extdata, so this vignette builds without a key and without a network. The code that made them is in vignette_results.R in the folder data-raw of the GitHub repository.

Microsoft-Decision-1 and Laya read text only. They are not in this vignette.

Image inputs

image takes one of these for each input:

  • a file path,
  • a URL,
  • a magick image, or a list of magick images.

text and image can go together. Element i of text and element i of image make input i. The package needs the magick package to read images. It turns each image upright, converts it to sRGB and sends it as a JPEG.

Data

The package has the dataset textiles. It has 50 simulated images of a woven textile, 250 x 250 pixels. They are in the folder system.file("extdata", "textiles", package = "decisions"). Half of them show a flaw in the pattern. See ?textiles for the details.

Source: the images come from the R package spc4sts. The public repository fmegahed/qe_genai shares them (MIT license, https://github.com/fmegahed/qe_genai).

Bui, A. T., & Apley, D. W. (2021). spc4sts: Statistical process control for stochastic textured surfaces in R. Journal of Quality Technology, 53(3), 219-242. https://doi.org/10.1080/00224065.2019.1707730

The CRAN page of spc4sts, which links its reference manual: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=spc4sts

textile_dir <- system.file("extdata", "textiles", package = "decisions")

textiles <- textiles |>
  dplyr::mutate(path = file.path(textile_dir, file))

dplyr::count(textiles, role, class)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   role      class         n
#>   <chr>     <fct>     <int>
#> 1 input     nominal      23
#> 2 input     defective    23
#> 3 reference nominal       2
#> 4 reference defective     2

The column role splits the images. Four images are references, two for each class. The other 46 images are the inputs. The column class is the truth.

The picture shows the four references. The top row has the two nominal images. The bottom row has the two defective images.

reference_files <- textiles |>
  dplyr::filter(role == "reference") |>
  dplyr::arrange(class, reference_rank)

reference_files$path |>
  magick::image_read() |>
  magick::image_montage(tile = "2x2", geometry = "250x250+4+4")

References

A reference is an image that shows what an answer looks like. references is a named list. Each name is an answer of the question. Each element has one or more images. The package prepares each reference once and sends it with every input.

references <- split(reference_files$path, reference_files$class)

inputs <- dplyr::filter(textiles, role == "input")

Question

One choice question has two answers. The descriptions are short. They say what the model sees.

weave <- question_choice(
  "Does the woven pattern in `inspection_image` have a flaw?",
  c(
    nominal = "The weave is regular. The pattern repeats with no break.",
    defective = "The weave has a flaw. A part of the pattern is broken, or the whole pattern is distorted."
  )
)

Image arguments

Three arguments set how the package prepares an image. They apply to the inputs and to the references.

Argument Meaning
max_size The longest side in pixels after the resize. The default is 768. NULL keeps the size.
upscale TRUE enlarges an image that is smaller than max_size. The default is FALSE.
crop "none" (default), "center" (a centered square), a box, or a function.

A box is c(x, y, width, height) in pixels. The origin is the top left of the image. The crop happens before the resize.

The textiles are 250 x 250 pixels. TypeSafe refuses images smaller than 280 pixels. So Jev needs upscale = TRUE. With max_size = 768, each image grows to 768 pixels.

Crop function

crop can be a function. It takes the magick image and returns a box. This is the hook for an object detection model. A detector would return the box of the object here, and the model would see the object only. The function below is simple: it trims a border of 12 pixels.

trim_border <- function(image) {
  info <- magick::image_info(image)
  c(12, 12, info$width - 24, info$height - 24)
}

Two hosted models

purrr::map() runs decide() once for each hosted decider. Each call sends 46 images. Each request holds the four references and one input.

deciders <- list(jev = decider_typesafe(), openai = decider_openai())

answers <- purrr::map(deciders, \(decider) {
  decide(
    decider, weave,
    image = inputs$path, references = references,
    max_size = 768, upscale = TRUE
  )
})

Clef-Flash

Clef-Flash is a model of Cloudflare. It runs on your computer, on a GPU, and it costs nothing per call. The shell command below starts a server with Docker. It is not run here. The image lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef holds SGLang. The first start downloads the model.

docker run --gpus all --shm-size 8g --ipc=host -p 30000:30000 \
  lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef \
  sglang serve --model-path Cloudflare/clef-flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

When GET http://localhost:30000/health answers, the server is ready. Clef-Flash reads the images in a list, so image_format = "images". The server needs no key. With a free model we can compare image settings: the same inputs with max_size = 768, with max_size = 512, and with the crop function.

clef <- decider_systemone(
  "http://localhost:30000", "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
  image_format = "images"
)

settings <- list(
  `max_size 768` = list(max_size = 768),
  `max_size 512` = list(max_size = 512),
  `crop trim` = list(max_size = 768, crop = trim_border)
)

clef_answers <- purrr::map(settings, \(setting) {
  rlang::exec(
    decide, clef, weave,
    image = inputs$path, references = references, upscale = TRUE,
    !!!setting
  )
})

Performance

We bind the tibbles and add the truth. Each tibble has 46 rows, in the order of the inputs. The levels of truth are nominal and defective. The event is the second level, so roc_auc_vec() gets event_level = "second".

all_answers <- c(answers, clef_answers)

results <- all_answers |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "model") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = names(all_answers)),
    truth = rep(inputs$class, times = length(all_answers))
  )

The next table has one row for each model and setting. roc_auc is the area under the ROC curve, from .pred_defective. errors is the number of rows with an error. A row with an error has NA answers, and yardstick removes it.

results |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    roc_auc = yardstick::roc_auc_vec(truth, .pred_defective, event_level = "second"),
    errors = sum(!is.na(.error)),
    input_tokens = sum(.input_tokens, na.rm = TRUE),
    cost_usd = if (all(is.na(.cost))) NA_real_ else sum(.cost, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_seconds = median(.seconds, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   model        roc_auc errors input_tokens cost_usd median_seconds
#>   <fct>          <dbl>  <int>        <dbl>    <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 jev            0.750      0       379638       NA          0.729
#> 2 openai         0.802      0       140530       NA          0.778
#> 3 max_size 768   0.831      0       142738       NA          3.89 
#> 4 max_size 512   0.830      0        69138       NA          1.83 
#> 5 crop trim      0.848      0       142738       NA          3.99

Forty-six images give a rough number only. One image changes the share of a class by 4 points. Use more images before you choose a model for real work.

Cost and time

TypeSafe, OpenAI and Clef-Flash report no cost, so .cost is NA, and decide() prints one message about it. All three report the input tokens. Each input holds four reference images, so the input tokens are many. .seconds is the time of one response. The requests run in parallel, so these times do not add up to the time of the whole call.

Settings

The three Clef-Flash rows differ in one setting. The roc_auc of the three is close: 0.83, 0.83 and 0.85. But Clef-Flash answered nominal for all 46 images in each run. Its probabilities rank the images, but the most likely answer is never defective. So a cut-off below 0.5 would be needed for this task. Jev answered defective for 14 images, and OpenAI for 9. Half of the images, 23, are defective.

A change of max_size changes the input tokens. The images at 512 pixels need about half the tokens of the images at 768 pixels, and the calls take about half the time. The roc_auc is the same to two digits. The crop function removes the border and changes the roc_auc by 0.02. With 46 images, we cannot say that this change is real. A setting that works for one model may not work for another. Test each setting on your own data, with images that you did not use to choose it.
